title: Chemical Bonding & Shapes of Molecules (VSEPR)
confusion: ❌ 'Ionic bonds are always stronger than covalent bonds.' ✅ Ionic bonds are strong in crystal lattices, but covalent bonds can be stronger in individual molecules (e.g., C≡C triple bond is very strong).
❌ 'VSEPR considers all electron pairs equally.' ✅ VSEPR accounts for different repulsion strengths: lp-lp > lp-bp > bp-bp, which distorts bond angles from ideal values.
❌ 'NH₃ is trigonal planar because it has 3 bond pairs.' ✅ NH₃ has 3 bp + 1 lp → tetrahedral electron geometry, but molecular shape is PYRAMIDAL (not planar) due to the lone pair.
❌ 'Hybridisation determines geometry; geometry determines hybridisation.' ✅ Hybridisation is a model used to *explain* observed geometries; it is not a physical process that happens before bonding.
notes: **Ionic bond:** electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions, formed by transfer of electrons (e.g. NaCl). High melting point, conducts electricity in molten/solution state.
**Covalent bond:** mutual sharing of electron pairs (e.g. H₂, CH₄). Directional; low melting/boiling point compared with ionic solids.
**Coordinate (dative) bond:** shared pair donated by one atom only (e.g. NH₄⁺, H₃O⁺).

**VSEPR theory:** electron pairs around the central atom repel each other and arrange to be as far apart as possible. Repulsion order: lone pair–lone pair > lone pair–bond pair > bond pair–bond pair.

Shapes: AX₂ linear (BeCl₂), AX₃ trigonal planar (BF₃), AX₄ tetrahedral (CH₄), AX₃E pyramidal (NH₃, 107°), AX₂E₂ bent (H₂O, 104.5°), AX₅ trigonal bipyramidal (PCl₅), AX₆ octahedral (SF₆).

**Hybridisation:** intermixing of orbitals of comparable energy to form equivalent hybrid orbitals — sp (linear, 180°), sp² (trigonal planar, 120°), sp³ (tetrahedral, 109.5°), sp³d (trigonal bipyramidal), sp³d² (octahedral).
